title: A US AI boom would lift growth well beyond tech sector
gist: Oxford Economics forecasts that sustained AI-driven tech capex will push US real gross output growth to ~4.2% by 2027 (over 1pp above baseline), with the gains spreading well beyond tech into construction, manufacturing, mining and professional services through 2029.

themes.theme: AI capex spillover to broader US economy

insights.claim: US real gross output growth could reach approximately 4.2% by 2027, more than one percentage point above baseline projections, driven by an AI-fueled boom.
insights.speaker: Keith Mason
insights.so_what: A materially above-trend growth path implies upside for broad US cyclical and equity exposure, not just AI/tech names, if the forecast holds.
insights.quote: By 2027, real gross output growth could reach approximately 4.2%, exceeding baseline projections by more than one percentage point.
insights.locator: An anticipated AI boom is set to significantly enhance growth

insights.claim: The growth boost is transmitted through sustained technology capital spending on computing capacity, data centres and software, which in turn lifts equity valuations and supports looser monetary policy, further stimulating investment and broader business activity.
insights.speaker: Keith Mason
insights.so_what: This is a transmission-mechanism framework linking AI capex to equity valuations and financial conditions, useful for tracing second-order effects of AI investment on rates and risk assets.
insights.locator: This growth is driven by a sustained increase in technology capital spending

insights.claim: Construction output is projected to rise around 6% above baseline by 2029, the largest uplift among major sectors, as AI adoption benefits spread across the economy.
insights.speaker: Keith Mason
insights.so_what: Construction (likely data-center and related infrastructure build-out) stands out as the single biggest relative beneficiary sector, ahead of tech itself, flagging it as a non-obvious AI-theme play.
insights.quote: construction output is projected to rise around 6% above baseline by 2029, marking the largest uplift among major sectors
insights.locator: As the benefits of AI adoption permeate various sectors

insights.claim: Mining and professional services are expected to see notable gains from increased investment and demand flowing through supply chains as the AI boom broadens.
insights.speaker: Keith Mason
insights.so_what: Identifies mining and professional services as secondary, supply-chain-linked beneficiaries of AI capex, sectors investors might not immediately associate with the AI theme.
insights.locator: Additionally, mining and professional services are expected to experience notable gains

insights.claim: Manufacturing output is expected to remain about 3% higher than baseline by 2029, with productivity gains sustaining the broader expansion even as monetary policy tightens to counter inflationary pressure.
insights.speaker: Keith Mason
insights.so_what: Implies the AI-driven growth uplift is expected to persist through a tightening cycle, so investors should watch whether productivity gains actually offset the drag from higher rates.
insights.quote: Manufacturing output is anticipated to remain around 3% higher by 2029, with broad-based gains across services and other industries.
insights.locator: Over time, productivity improvements will help maintain this expansion
